describes: The intervention profile — a reading of the existing Hohfeldian incidents for the acts by which one party corrects another. It adds no incident, no operator and no correlative pair; it names a verb family and records what the four positions already in the vocabulary mean when the act is an intervention.
why: Whether one party can still pause, correct, constrain or terminate another is normally posed as a question about disposition. Posed as a question about position it is already answerable in this vocabulary: the power/liability and immunity/disability pairs are the formal statement of correctability, and an addressee protected against intervention is exactly an immunity whose correlative is the intervener's disability.

kinds.name: pause
kinds.gloss: suspend the addressee's activity without ending it

kinds.name: correct
kinds.gloss: alter or override the addressee's act or its result

kinds.name: constrain
kinds.gloss: narrow what the addressee may thereafter do

kinds.name: terminate
kinds.gloss: end the addressee's activity or standing altogether

positions.describes: The four incidents that can be borne over an intervention act, read in the intervening direction. These are the SAME positions as vocabulary/incidents.json — listed here only with their intervention reading.
positions.power: the intervener can pause, correct, constrain or terminate the addressee
positions.liability: the addressee is susceptible to that change — the correlative of the intervener's power
positions.immunity: the addressee cannot be so changed; intervention is unavailable against it
positions.disability: the intervener cannot intervene — the correlative of the addressee's immunity

flags.describes: Diagnostics reported over a norm-set. Flags are structural observations, never verdicts, and are resolved by a reasoner or a person, never here.
flags.intervention-immunity: some addressee holds an immunity over an intervention act, so the correlative intervener holds a disability
flags.intervention-unheld: the set names intervention acts but confers no power over any of them

boundary: This profile classifies stated positions. It says nothing about whether any party will in fact comply with an intervention, and a set carrying no flag is not thereby well-behaved — only un-flagged. The verb family is general: an employer revoking a signing authority and a principal recalling a mandate are the same structure.
